reviews.text: Worldcoin is a biometric ID project with the WLD token for universal basic income, launched in 2023 by Tools for Humanity. It uses orb scanners for proof-of-personhood. In 2025, it has faced privacy backlash but has millions of users. The team is led by Sam Altman. It’s visionary but controversial.

Worldcoin is Sam Altman’s ambitious crypto identity project using “Orbs” for ids sign-up, scanning the human as a proof of person. Participants get free WLD tokens. In the last period it attracted controversy and slow growth: regulatory crackdowns in countries like Colombia and the Philippines have temporarily halted orbs. Some complaints about the security of the stored data came from Spain and China as well. Its user base (a bit more than 17.5M people since 2019) is far below the 1B+ goal sponsored by the company at the beginning. The WLD token itself is semi-lockup locked (42% locked) and had a high price drop from maximum. From my point of view: Worldcoin promises a network with verified humans with encrypted data plus a currency, but adoption is quite behind hype. It’s raising $500M funds and uses Orb scans, yet there are many concerns related to privacy issues and centralization (as it is governed by Tools for Humanity).

World coin is crypto token and complex dapp that aims to provide incentives for users that provide their biometric in order to acquire a digital identity such that real humans are distinguished from AI bots by using proof of person hood consensus. The project has a greater goal of providing universal basic income for everyone. It was originally built on Optimism, but now they have created and migrated to their own layer 2  called world chain. The project is founded by Sam Altman, Open AI CEO and with backing of top tier VCs like a16z. The is high controversy about the project especially regarding centralization and privacy concern.

Worldcoin feels very futuristic the idea of giving people a unique crypto ID via an iris scan is groundbreaking. I appreciate its ambition and the fact that it’s gotten millions to sign up with its orb devices. Still, I’m personally uneasy about the privacy trade offs. Letting a crypto project scan your eyeball strikes me as a bold move that governments and privacy advocates are rightly nervous about.

I evaluated Worldcoin, a highly ambitious identity focused crypto project that uses iris scanning hardware “Orbs” to verify real humans and issue a unique digital identity called World ID. The project aims to solve the growing problem of bots, fake accounts, and Sybil attacks by tying identity verification to biometric data. While the vision is big, the approach raises major concerns around privacy, centralization, and regulatory scrutiny. As of 2025, adoption remains limited outside early testers, and the long term viability depends on whether the project can earn public trust and expand real utility around its identity system.
